steps.title: An open barrel with a sticky rim
steps.text: GroEL is two rings of seven subunits. Each subunit's apical domain lines the mouth of the ring, and its inner face is hydrophobic — a sticky surface for unfolded proteins.

steps.title: Unfolded protein docks at the rim
steps.text: An unfolded chain exposes hydrophobic patches and binds across several apical domains at the mouth. It sits at the rim, not floating above the barrel — that is the view you see here.

labels.text: substrate held at the apical tips

steps.title: ATP binds the equator — the engine
steps.text: Every subunit has an ATP site in its equatorial domain, ~70 Å from the substrate. ATP binding is cooperative: the seven sites of one ring fill together. This is what powers everything that follows.

steps.title: ATP swings the apical domains
steps.text: ATP closes the equatorial cleft and the apical domains swing upward and inward — the twist here is a morph between the open and closed crystal structures, not a whole-ring spin. The hydrophobic tips release the chain into the cavity, and a new surface appears: the GroES-binding interface.

steps.title: GroES docks on that interface
steps.text: GroES — seven subunits — binds only the ATP-loaded ring, because ATP created the surface it grips. The lid encloses the cavity and flips its lining from hydrophobic to hydrophilic. Only one ring is capped at a time: the symmetric two-cap “football” is an in-vitro side state, not the working cycle.

steps.title: Folding inside, hydrolysis as the timer
steps.text: The protein folds in isolation, shielded from aggregation. Meanwhile the seven ATPs in this ring hydrolyze to ADP + Pi. Hydrolysis weakens the GroES interface — it is the clock, not the folding machine.

steps.title: The cage opens; the other ring fires
steps.text: GroES dissociates and the folded protein leaves. The other ring is not idle: it has already bound substrate and ATP, and its ATP binding is what helps pry the lid off this ring. Then it becomes the capped ring — the two rings alternate, one ATP cycle each.

steps.title: Roles swap — the loop restarts
steps.text: The old cis ring is now trans: it releases ADP and binds fresh substrate and ATP. The ring that was waiting becomes cis and gets capped in turn. Same machine, roles exchanged.
